summary: Fluconazole is a triazole antifungal for vaginal, oropharyngeal, esophageal, urinary, and systemic candidiasis, cryptococcal meningitis, and candidiasis prophylaxis in bone marrow transplant patients. Oral absorption is rapid and nearly complete, so oral and IV doses are the same.
indications: Candida urinary tract infections, peritonitis, and systemic Candida infections (candidemia, disseminated candidiasis, pneumonia)
Prophylaxis of candidiasis in bone marrow transplant patients receiving cytotoxic chemotherapy and/or radiation

200 mg day 1, then 100 mg once daily
200 mg day 1, then 100 mg once daily (up to 400 mg/day)
dosage.t: At least 3 weeks and >=2 weeks after symptom resolution

dosage.d: Up to 400 mg/day (loading dose twice the daily dose on day 1)
400 mg day 1, then 200-400 mg once daily; maintenance/suppression 200 mg once daily
dosage.n: AIDS patients require maintenance to prevent relapse

admin: Obtain fungal cultures/specimens before starting therapy
May be given orally or IV with the same dose (oral bioavailability >90%)
Give a loading dose of twice the daily dose on day 1 for multiple-dose regimens

Reduce maintenance dose in renal impairment for multiple-dose regimens
moa: Fluconazole selectively inhibits fungal cytochrome P450 sterol 14-alpha-demethylase, blocking conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol. The resulting ergosterol depletion and accumulation of toxic sterol precursors damages the fungal cell membrane, inhibiting fungal growth.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to fluconazole or its excipients
Coadministration with QT-prolonging CYP3A4 substrates: erythromycin, pimozide, quinidine (contraindicated)

preg: Avoid in pregnancy except for severe/life-threatening fungal infection where benefit outweighs risk. High-dose maternal use (400-800 mg/day) in the first trimester is associated with a pattern of congenital anomalies. A single 150 mg dose is considered low risk. Use effective contraception with high-dose therapy.
lact: Fluconazole is present in breast milk at low levels (estimated infant dose ~0.39 mg/kg/day after a single 150 mg dose, ~13% of pediatric oropharyngeal dose). Generally considered compatible with breastfeeding.
renal: For multiple-dose therapy, give the usual loading dose, then reduce the maintenance dose by ~50% if CrCl <=50 mL/min. Hemodialysis patients: give the usual dose after each dialysis session. Single-dose vaginal candidiasis needs no adjustment.
hepatic: Use with caution; rare cases of serious (including fatal) hepatotoxicity have occurred. Monitor LFTs and discontinue if clinical signs/symptoms of liver disease develop.

major: QT-prolonging CYP3A4 substrates (erythromycin, pimozide, quinidine - contraindicated)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid due to additive hepatotoxicity risk.

monitoring: Liver function tests at baseline and periodically
ECG and electrolytes in QT risk patients
counsel: May take with or without food

Inform clinician of all medications (many interactions)
Use effective contraception with high-dose therapy
pk: Rapid absorption; clinical response over days
pearls: Oral bioavailability >90%; oral and IV doses are identical
Long half-life (~30 hr) supports once-daily dosing and a day-1 loading dose
Single 150 mg dose acceptable in pregnancy; high-dose chronic use is teratogenic
Potent CYP2C9/CYP3A4 inhibitor - strong warfarin and sulfonylurea interactions
missed: Take as soon as remembered; if near the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not double up. (Single-dose regimens: not applicable.)
overdose: Reported with supportive care; hallucinations and paranoid behavior reported at very high doses. A 3-hour hemodialysis session reduces plasma levels by ~50%. Manage symptomatically.
